Application Materials.content:
As part of your online application you will need to upload scanned documents. All academic documentation should be scans of the originals, not photographs. The scans should be complete and of a good quality, showing the 4 corners of all pages of the original document. Please do not merge separate qualifications together. Supporting documents should always be sent via an enquiry or condition response in the applicant portal.
Your application must include:
- A copy of your degree certificate and complete transcript. If you are still studying, provide your latest transcript plus a list of modules yet to be studied.
- Evidence of your final or current overall % or GPA.
- A copy of your grading scale/scheme if this is not on your degree transcript.
- CV/Resume: include an up-to-date CV showing your relevant work experience and education.
- CAS, BRP and Visa, for international students that have previously studied in the UK on a student visa.
- If you entered your current degree programme later than year 1, include separate details of the qualification used to gain entry into that later year of your degree, including any transcripts and certificates for that qualification.
If you have them, include:
- Your approved English Language test, if applicable.
- A personal statement. A personal statement is not required as standard, but could strengthen your application in circumstances such as explaining a gap in your education or showing relevance if your education/degree subject is not directly relevant to the programme. The personal statement should be **no more than one side of A4** and should include details on how your prior studies are linked to your future plans and why you want to study the programme you have applied for.
Documents which are not required:
- References are not usually required, but in specific borderline cases a reference may be required to help make a decision.
Country-specific documentation:
- Applicants with Chinese degrees: provide evidence of your current/final overall weighted percentage (%).
- Applicants with Indian degrees: include a copy of your bachelor’s degree certificate; a copy of your consolidated mark sheet; a copy of your semester mark sheets; a copy of your University marking scheme; and official evidence of your current/final overall award as a percentage (%). If you have not completed your degree, provide the bottom three items.
- Applicants with Canadian degrees: provide details of the grading system used on your transcript, including the percentage pass mark for your degree. If your degree was taught in English, include official evidence of this.

Interview Requirements.content: We aim to make decisions within **three to five weeks** if all necessary documents have been received. You will be contacted directly if we require any further information or wish to invite you for an interview or audition. You will receive an email asking you to check your applicant portal for more details.

Application Deadlines.content:
- Start date: **September 2026**.
- Application deadlines: **31 July 2026** – International applicants; **11 September 2026** – UK applicants.
- Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.

Academic Requirements.content:
A bachelor degree with a **2:1 (hons) in computer science**. Applicants must have studied a breadth of relevant modules including **significant programming, systems development, data structures and algorithms**.
Applicants with any of the following will be considered on a case-by-case basis:
- A bachelor degree with a **2:1 (hons) in other computing-based degrees**.
- A bachelor degree with a **2:2 (hons) in computer science**, with **at least three years of relevant experience**.
- Professional qualifications and relevant experience.
International applicants: Leeds accepts a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/admissions-qualifications).
Applicants from China: accepted qualifications include **4 year Bachelor degrees**. The University of Leeds uses institutional lists when assessing applications from accepted Chinese institutions, and requirements may vary by school; applicants should check that their institution is accepted and that they meet the entry requirements before applying. If the programme asks for **2.1**, applicants from China need **70%-85%, depending on institution**. If the programme asks for **2.2**, applicants from China need **70%-80%, depending on institution**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
IELTS **6.5 overall**, with no less than **6.0 in any component**. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").
International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study a postgraduate pre-sessional English course, designed with a progression route to the degree programme. Relevant options include [Language for Engineering (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i193/language-for-engineering), [Language for Science: Engineering (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i194/language-for-science-engineering), the [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-), the [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-), and longer [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).

Program Overview.content:
Start date September 2026. Delivery type On campus. Duration 12 Months (Full time).
From science to marketing, engineering to medicine, big data has become crucial to a wide range of industries. Many organisations are keen to employ qualified experts in computing who have a particular focus in data. The Advanced Computer Science (Data Analytics) MSc will equip you with specialist knowledge in this field and allow you to explore a range of advanced topics in computer science. You’ll gain a foundation in topics like data science, as well as the basics of machine learning and knowledge representation, and can broaden your approach with topics like cloud computing.
Studying in the [School of Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing) gives you access to specialist facilities, whilst being taught by academics who are experts in their fields. The School has internationally excellent research and long-established links in industry and with the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) (LIDA), which is at the forefront of big data research. The University is also partnered with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and artificial intelligence.
In the first half of the year, you’ll study core modules which lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of key topics of data science, cloud computing and machine learning. From there you’ll tailor your studies through optional modules on diverse topics such as deep learning, knowledge representation, blockchain technologies, data mining and text analytics. In the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll work on a research project as an integral part of one of the School’s active research groups, focusing on a specialist topic in computer science and selecting appropriate research methods. A proportion of projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.
The course gives you the chance to build industry experience by conducting an individual project focused on a real-world topic of your choice, developing professional skills in research and critical thinking. You’ll access industry-standard specialist facilities including a state-of-the-art cloud computing lab, a large High Performance Computing (HPC) resource, robotics labs, a state-of-the-art computing cluster with access to Azure services and GPU computing, high-performance graphics workstations, dedicated Linux laboratories with a combined capacity of an average of 150 machines, and facilities and teaching spaces in the Sir William Henry Bragg building.
The programme team includes expert academics, from lecturers through to professors, specialising in a wide range of computing topics. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers. The School’s research feeds directly into teaching, and you’ll have regular contact with staff through lectures, seminars, tutorials, small group work and project meetings. Independent study is also important to the programme, as you develop your problem-solving and research skills as well as your subject knowledge.
You’ll be assessed using a range of techniques which may include case studies, technical reports, group work, presentations, in-class tests, assignments and exams. Optional modules may also use alternative assessment methods.
Computing is an essential component of nearly every daily activity, from the collection and processing of information in business, through to smart systems embedded in devices, image processing in medical diagnosis and the middleware that underpins distributed technologies like cloud computing and the semantic web. This programme will give you the practical skills to enter many areas of applied computing, working as application developers, system designers and evaluators. Links between the taught modules and research provide students with added strengths in artificial intelligence, intelligent systems, distributed systems, and the analysis of complex data. Graduates will be well-prepared for a range of careers, as well as further research at PhD level.
The University of Leeds is in the top 5 most targeted universities in the UK by graduate recruiters, according to [High Fliers’ The Graduate Market in 2024 report](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/747999993/). Job positions and organisations previous advanced computer science graduates have secured include Engineer at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, Senior Software Engineer at Funding Circle, Technical Developer at Reading Room, Head of Audience Development at Al Jazeera Media Network, Systems Engineer at Systematic, Software Engineer at THG, Programmer at Alibaba, and PhD candidate at Monash University.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. The work experience is formally integrated into your degree, enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience.

Curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
In the first half of the year, you'll study core modules which will lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of the key topics of data science, cloud computing and machine learning. From there you’ll have the chance to tailor your studies to suit your own preferences. You’ll choose from a wide range of optional modules on diverse topics such as deep learning, knowledge representation, blockchain technologies, data mining and text analytics. In the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll also work on your research project.
The list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time.
Compulsory modules:
- **Data Science – 15 credits**: The aim of the module is for you to understand methods of analysis that allow people to gain insights from complex data.
- **Cloud Computing Systems – 15 credits**: The module aims to develop a practical understanding of methods, techniques and architectures needed to build big data systems, so that knowledge can be extracted from large, diverse data sets.
- **Machine learning - 15 credits**: This module covers topics selected from: Decision trees, Bayesian networks, instance-based learning, kernel machines, clustering, reinforcement learning inductive logic programming, artificial neural networks, deep learning.
- **MSc Project – 60 credits**: You’ll undertake a research project during the summer months. The professional project allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem. Recent projects include Text mining of e-health patient records; Java-based visualisation on ultra-high resolution displays; Data mining of sports performance data. A proportion of projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.
Optional modules listed are indicative of typical options:
- **Blockchain Technologies – 15 credits**
- **Knowledge Representation and Reasoning – 15 credits**
- **Deep Learning – 15 credits**
- **Algorithms – 15 credits**
- **Programming for Data Science – 15 credits**
- **Data Mining and Text Analytics – 15 credits**
- **Advanced Software Engineering – 15 credits**
- **Scientific Computation – 15 credits**
- **Graph Theory: Structure and Algorithms – 15 credits**
As part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0). [For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Computer Science (Data Analytics) MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-ACS%2FD-FT).
You’ll be assessed using a range of techniques which may include case studies, technical reports, group work, presentations, in-class tests, assignments and exams. Optional modules may also use alternative assessment methods.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. This work experience is formally integrated into your degree, enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The information is provided as a guideline only, based on average spending. The following tables are estimates for a single student in 2025 based on the latest data available. The actual amount will depend on your accommodation type and availability, and your lifestyle. They don’t include tuition fees.
| Accommodation | Estimated cost per week |
| --- | --- |
| University accommodation, self-catered | £117 to £265 |
| University accommodation, catered | £205 to £273 |
| Private accommodation, self-catered | £110 to £300 (costs may be more for higher specifications) |
| Living expenses | Estimated cost per week |
| --- | --- |
| Groceries: food, toiletries and cleaning products | £31 to £38 |
| Household bills: gas and/or electricity, water and broadband internet (these are included in most university accommodation and some private accommodation) | £14 to £17 |
| Personal costs: transport, socialising, restaurants/takeaways, clothes and mobile phone | £44 to £68 |
**Estimated total budget per week: approximately £199 to £423**
